sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 7.7% a year from $15.4 billion in FY2018 to $25.8 billion in FY2025 [F1][F8][F145], while operating income grew faster at 9.9% [F146] and net income barely moved at 0.4% [F147].
The window is not a smooth compounder: operating margin swung from 30.6% in FY2019 to 15.5% in FY2021, then to 41.3% in FY2023 and 32.1% in FY2025 [F18][F20][F22][F24].
The FY2021 collapse came with a 43.1% fall in operating income [D97], and the FY2020 filing attributes the prior-year NEER decline to a roughly $1.5 billion Mountain Valley Pipeline impairment [P68].
The FY2023 spike reflects NEER's swing to $3.56 billion of net income [S27], which the FY2024 filing attributes to favorable non-qualifying hedge activity compared with 2023 [P36].
FPL remains the revenue base at 70.5% of FY2025 revenue [D271], contributing 5.5pp of the 9.8% revenue growth [D273][D236].
FPL's $1.24 billion revenue increase came from higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan revenues, partly offset by lower fuel cost recovery [P21].
Operating costs grew 10.0% against 9.8% revenue growth in FY2025 [D249][D236], so incremental operating margin was only 34.8% [D256].
NEER's segment net income rose to $2.98 billion [S29], which the filing attributes to higher earnings from new wind, solar and battery investments, partly offset by higher financing costs [P26].
Diluted EPS fell 0.7% a year over the window [F149] while net income rose 0.4% [F147], as the diluted share count grew 0.6% in FY2025 alone [D251].
FY2025 operating margin of 32.1% [F24] sits 1.8pp above the 30.3% window median [D300] and far below the 41.3% FY2023 high [D299].
D&A rose to 25.5% of revenue in FY2025 from 23.2% in FY2024 [D224][D189], and the filing attributes the $951 million increase mainly to higher storm-cost amortization and plant in service [P16].
Net margin fell 3.1pp to 26.5% [F40][D248], 5.6pp below operating margin [D327], as other expense reached $3.75 billion [X64].
Corporate and Other's results fell $1.26 billion, mainly from about $1.0 billion of unfavorable non-qualifying interest-rate hedge activity and higher average debt balances [P8].
The effective tax rate turned negative at -17.7% [D226], which the filing attributes to clean energy tax credits that rose about $585 million [P11].
Operating cash flow of $12.5 billion was 1.83x net income in FY2025 [F64][F32][D227], below the 1.95x window median [D319].
Investing outflow of $23.9 billion [F72] dwarfed operating cash flow, so free cash flow was deeply negative and the gap was funded by $13.0 billion of net financing [F80].
The filing notes that a shift from net over-recovery to net under-recovery of cost recovery clauses cut FPL's operating cash flow by about $89 million [P19].
Stock-based compensation is immaterial to cash at 1.5% of operating cash flow [D228], so conversion is driven by working capital and the capital programme, not equity pay.
Total debt reached $95.0 billion in FY2025 [D230], leaving net debt of $92.2 billion [D231], equal to 357.4% of revenue [D232].
That net-debt ratio ranks at the 0th percentile of the three-peer utilities group, against a peer median net debt of 235.4% of revenue [D328][D329].
Liquidity is thin: cash of $2.81 billion [F96] against a 0.60x current ratio [F128], the window high but still below 1.0x [D305].
Dividends of $4.68 billion [X82] were the main capital return, with no buybacks evident, while debt issued of $23.4 billion [X90] funded the $23.9 billion investing outflow [F72].
The current ratio has stayed below 1.0x every year, at 0.60x in FY2025 [F128][D304], a structural feature of a utility funding long-lived assets with short-term liabilities rather than a new stress.
Net debt has risen for seven consecutive years to $92.2 billion [D231][R2], and long-term debt grew 23.7% in FY2025 alone [D245], the fastest pace in the window.
Revenue fell 5.2% in FY2024 [D201][R3], which the FY2024 filing attributes to lower storm and fuel cost recovery revenues [P35].
The effective tax rate swung -23.3pp to -17.7% in FY2025 [D226][R4], making net margin dependent on clean energy credits rather than operating results.
Watch operating margin against the 30.3% window median [D300]: a print below it in the FY2026 10-K would confirm the post-FY2023 fade, while a return toward the 41.3% high [D299] would reverse it.
Watch net debt, now $92.2 billion [D231]: further growth at the FY2025 pace of 15.7% [D253] would extend the seven-year streak, while any decline would break it.
Watch operating cash flow against the 1.95x net-income median [D319]: a print below the 0.99x window low [D318] would signal conversion deterioration.
